1.w: Do not be envious of men of evil, and do not desire to be with them,

2.w: for their heart devises violence and their lips speak trouble.

3.w: By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established,

4.w: and by knowledge the rooms are filled with all precious pleasant wealth.

5.w: A man of wisdom [is] strong; and a man of knowledge strengthens power;

6.w: for by wise counsel you can fashion for yourself the battle, and victory [is] in a multitude counselors.

7.w: Wisdom [is] high for a fool; in the gate he does not open his mouth.

8.w: One planning to do evil, they will call him an owner of schemes.

9.w: The plotting of foolishness [is] sin, and an abomination to man [is] onemocking.

10.w: [If] you slacken in the day of distress, [then] narrow [is] your strength.

11.w: Deliver those being led away to death, and those stumbling to the slaughter, if only you would hold back.

12.w: If you say, “Behold we did not know this,” does not the One weighing hearts Himself know [it], and the One watching over your soul Himself know it? And He has rendered to each man according to his work.

13.w: Eat honey, my son, for [it is] good, and the honeycomb [is] sweet upon your palate.

14.w: Know that wisdom [is] thus to your soul; if you have found [it], then there is a posterity, and your hope will not be cut off.

15.w: Do not lie in wait like a wicked one against the abode of the righteous; do not spoil his resting place;

16.w: for seven times the righteous may fall and rise up, and the wicked shall stumble into evil.

17.w: At the falling of your enemy, you should not be glad, and in his stumbling do not let your heart rejoice,

18.w: lest YHWH should see and [it be] evil in His eyes, and He turns away His anger from him.

19.w: You must not fret at the evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked,

20.w: for there is no posterity for an evil one, [and] the lamp of the wicked ones will be extinguished.

21.w: Fear YHWH, my son, and the king; do not pledge yourself with ones who change,

22.w: for suddenly their downfall will arise, and the ruin of them both—who knows?

23.w: These also are of the wise ones: The recognizing of faces in [giving] judgment [is] not good.

24.w: One saying to a wicked one, “You [are] righteous”—peoples will curse him; nations will denounce him;

25.w: and to those reproving it will be pleasant, and upon them will come a blessing of goodness.

26.w: The lips he kisses—the one returning straightforward words.

27.w: Prepare your work in the outdoors, and make it ready in the field for yourself; and afterward you may build your house.

28.w: You must not be a witness without cause against your neighbor or deceive with your lips.

29.w: Do not say, “According to what he has done to me, so I will do to him; I will return to the man according to his deed.”

30.w: Near the field of a lazy man I passed by, and near the vineyard of a man lacking heart.

31.w: And behold, thorns had come up all over it; its face was covered with nettles, and the wall of its stones was torn down.

32.w: And I saw—I—I set my heart; I have seen, I have received instruction.

33.w: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little a folding of the hands to rest,

34.w: and your poverty has come [as] one traveling, and your needs like a man of shield.
